phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.description: Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens is Schenley Park's ticketed glasshouse and garden complex, with changing exhibits, its own schedule, visitor parking, cafe, restrooms and accessibility services.
phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.location: Use Phipps' GPS locator address, 700 Frank Curto Drive, for the Welcome Center. The conservatory sits beside Schenley Drive and Flagstaff Hill, not at the broad Schenley Park or Schenley Oval pin.
phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.parking: Phipps provides free visitor parking in the Schenley Drive center island, metered spaces on both sides, and accessible spaces near the entrance. Panther Hollow and Charles Anderson bridges are closed to vehicles, so follow the operator's current detours and allow extra time.
phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.hours: Open Monday-Thursday 9:30 a.m.-5 p.m., Friday 9:30 a.m.-10 p.m., and Saturday-Sunday 9:30 a.m.-5 p.m. Last entry is 30 minutes before closing; shows and visitor notices can close individual areas.
phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.restrooms: Visitor restrooms are inside the staffed conservatory. Phipps' sensory guide identifies restroom and quiet-space locations; do not rely on building facilities before admission or after closing.
phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.fees: Current general admission is $22.95 for adults, $20.95 for ages 62+, $19.95 for students 19+, and $13.95 for ages 2-18; members and children under 2 are free. Eligible EBT guests may receive Museums for All admission for up to four people at $3 each.
phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.accessibility: Most gardens are wheelchair accessible except the Stove Room. Manual wheelchairs and sensory bags are available free first-come at admissions, and accessible parking is near the entrance; stone and concrete paths can be uneven or slippery.
phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.dogs: Pets are not allowed inside Phipps. ADA-defined service animals are permitted.
phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.family: Allow roughly 90 minutes to two hours for a self-guided visit. Indoor and outdoor gardens work in mixed weather, but rooms vary in temperature and large bags, wagons and outside food are restricted.
phipps-conservatory-and-botanical-garden.need: Advance timed tickets are strongly recommended and required during Holiday Magic. Tickets are nonrefundable, re-entry is not permitted, and nearby bridge closures change the normal driving approach.

schenley-plaza.description: Schenley Plaza is the park's level Oakland gathering lawn, carousel and food-stop zone between Carnegie Library, Phipps and the university district.
schenley-plaza.sourceLabel: Pittsburgh Parks Conservancy Schenley entrances guide
schenley-plaza.location: Navigate to Schenley Plaza at Forbes Avenue and Schenley Drive. It is the north Oakland edge of the larger park, across from Carnegie Library and downhill from Flagstaff Hill.
schenley-plaza.parking: The Conservancy identifies parallel and head-in street parking around the plaza. Read meter and event restrictions carefully; university activity and Phipps traffic can fill the immediate spaces.
schenley-plaza.hours: The outdoor plaza follows posted City park hours. The PNC Carousel, The Porch, kiosks, rentals and events use separate seasonal or daily schedules.
schenley-plaza.restrooms: Do not assume an always-open public restroom in the lawn. Use an open staffed plaza business, library, museum or Phipps only under that operator's access rules and hours.
schenley-plaza.fees: Ordinary lawn, seating and path access is free. Carousel rides, food, rentals and ticketed or reserved events cost separately.
schenley-plaza.accessibility: The central plaza has broad paved walks and a relatively level lawn-edge route, but curb cuts, temporary event furniture, grass and crowding can affect movement.
schenley-plaza.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor plaza areas under City rules. Keep pets out of food-service seating, the carousel and any posted or event-controlled zone.
schenley-plaza.family: The open lawn, seasonal carousel and nearby food can make an easy family stop. Confirm carousel operation and plan a restroom before settling in.
schenley-plaza.need: Treat the plaza, carousel and food operators as separate schedules. A quiet lawn visit can change quickly during university events, festivals or rentals.

panther-hollow-lake.description: Panther Hollow Lake is the small man-made lake beneath the park's bridges, reached by trail and steps rather than as a drive-up waterfront destination.
panther-hollow-lake.address: Panther Hollow Trail, Schenley Park, Pittsburgh, PA 15213
panther-hollow-lake.sourceLabel: Pittsburgh Parks Conservancy Schenley entrances guide
panther-hollow-lake.location: The lake sits below Phipps, Flagstaff Hill and Panther Hollow Road. Anderson Playground is a practical upper arrival for steps down toward the lake; use the exact lake pin and expect a climb back out.
panther-hollow-lake.parking: Use legal two-hour parking near Anderson Playground or another mapped Schenley entrance, then continue on foot. There is no lakefront parking lot and closed bridges can alter vehicle circulation.
panther-hollow-lake.hours: Visit the lake and connecting natural trails in daylight under posted park and trail rules. Flooding, mud, ice, fallen trees and maintenance can close or complicate the approach.
panther-hollow-lake.restrooms: There is no dependable restroom at the lake. Use an open staffed facility before descending into Panther Hollow.
panther-hollow-lake.fees: Trail and lake-view access is free. This is not a staffed boating, swimming or rental facility.
panther-hollow-lake.accessibility: The hollow approach includes steep grades, steps and natural surfaces and is not a step-free lake visit. Choose Schenley Plaza or another developed park destination when a firm level route is essential.
panther-hollow-lake.dogs: Leashed dogs may use open trails under City rules. Keep animals out of the water and under close control on steep, muddy and narrow sections.
panther-hollow-lake.family: The lake can be a short nature destination for trail-ready children, but steep access, rail infrastructure, water and limited facilities require close supervision.
panther-hollow-lake.need: This is a trail destination, not a swimming lake or drive-up picnic area. Download the park map, visit in daylight and avoid the hollow during thunderstorms, flooding, snow or ice.

flagstaff-hill.description: Flagstaff Hill is the broad slope and skyline viewpoint directly above Phipps, used for picnics, sledding, films and informal gatherings.
flagstaff-hill.sourceLabel: Pittsburgh Parks Conservancy Schenley entrances guide
flagstaff-hill.location: Flagstaff Hill rises across Schenley Drive from Phipps and southeast of Schenley Plaza. Use the exact hill pin rather than routing to the Oval or Panther Hollow Lake.
flagstaff-hill.parking: Use legal spaces along Schenley Drive and the Phipps area, honoring meters, bike-lane markings and event restrictions. Phipps visitor spaces are intended for conservatory guests, not an all-day hill visit.
flagstaff-hill.hours: Use the open hill during posted City park hours. Films, festivals, university events, snow conditions and maintenance can create separate access or crowd controls.
flagstaff-hill.restrooms: There is no dependable dedicated restroom on the hill. Phipps restrooms require admission and follow conservatory hours; plan another open facility before arriving.
flagstaff-hill.fees: Ordinary hill, picnic and skyline-view access is free. Permitted events, food and nearby attractions may charge separately.
flagstaff-hill.accessibility: The defining lawn is sloped and grassy. Paved roadside viewpoints may provide partial context, but the hill itself is not a level or uniformly firm destination.
flagstaff-hill.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the open hill under City rules. Avoid event-controlled areas and clean up waste on the heavily shared lawn.
flagstaff-hill.family: The skyline, open grass and proximity to Phipps make a flexible family stop. Supervise children beside Schenley Drive and on the steep slope, especially during snow or crowded events.
flagstaff-hill.need: Bring shade and water in summer and traction in winter. The open slope is exposed to sun, wind, lightning and snow, and event programming can replace normal informal use.
